abstract: Education for Sustainable Development (ESD) is a contemporary issue in the present world as it helps to achieve a sustainable future for mankind at a local and global level. This study explores the perspective of pre-service secondary teacher educators regarding ESD and the importance of incorporating ESD into the pre-service teacher education programme. A quantitative approach was adopted for this investigation, followed by a self-developed questionnaire with open-ended and closed-ended questions. A survey through different online platforms gathered information about the perspective and understanding of pre-service secondary teacher educators on this issue. The major finding of the study was that most of the pre-service secondary teachers had some understanding of environmental aspects but did not consider socio-cultural or economic matters to be the aspects of ESD. For the most part, ESD was primarily concerned with various environmental issues and their management. Furthermore, half of the participants had never had lessons on ESD during their formal education, but most of them agreed that inclusion of ESD in teacher education needs specific teaching approaches. Altogether, the results showed that pre-service secondary teacher educators strongly believe in the significant importance of ESD in teacher education. In conclusion, we can say that including Education for Sustainable development in the pre-service secondary teacher education programme would immediately boost teacher educators’ abilities to teach prospective teachers about sustainability and contribute to our country's progress toward a sustainable future

title: PERSPECTIVE OF PRE-SERVICE SECONDARY TEACHER EDUCATORS ON EDUCATION FOR SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT: AN EXPLORATION
